sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and the Pitfalls of 'Pseudo-angioedema'
sections.description: This section explores the initial presentation of the patient, the common pitfalls in diagnosing neck swelling, and how dermatomyositis can masquerade as more common emergency or immunological conditions.
subtopics: Evaluating acute and subacute neck swelling: Differential diagnosis
Ludwig's angina: Clinical features and CT imaging characteristics
Distinguishing between histaminergic, bradykinin-mediated, and non-immune mediated oedema
Recognizing atypical presentation: The significance of a 3-week progressive course without fever
The role of nasendoscopy in excluding anatomical or obstructive causes of swelling

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Reasoning: Pivoting from Localized to Systemic Disease
sections.description: This section teaches the clinician how to transition from a narrow focus on a single symptom (neck swelling) to a systemic search for a diagnosis through careful physical examination and targeted laboratory tests.
subtopics: The 'Red Flags' of angioedema: When a patient's profile is atypical for hereditary or acquired angioedema
The importance of a comprehensive skin and nail exam: Identifying periungual telangiectasias and subtle rashes
Clinical signs of proximal muscle weakness: Assessing hip flexor power
The diagnostic utility of Creatine Kinase (CK) and transaminases (ALT/AST) in suspected myopathy
Interpreting the relationship between muscle inflammation and subcutaneous soft tissue oedema

sections.description: This section details the comprehensive investigation required to confirm a diagnosis of dermatomyositis, focusing on the specificity of autoantibodies, imaging, and histopathology.
subtopics: Serological markers: ANA patterns and the myositis-specific antibody panel
The significance of anti-SAE1 antibodies and their clinical associations
Advanced imaging for myositis: MRI vs. FDG-PET scan in detecting active muscle inflammation
Muscle biopsy: Identifying perifascicular atrophy and C5b-9 complement deposition
Evaluating systemic involvement: Pulmonary function tests for restrictive patterns and Barium swallow for pharyngeal dysphagia

sections.description: This section explains the underlying biological mechanisms of dermatomyositis and the specific role of the SAE1 enzyme, providing the necessary medical background to understand the disease's behavior.
subtopics: The general pathophysiology of Dermatomyositis: Capillary destruction and myofibre necrosis
The SUMO pathway: Understanding the Small Ubiquitin-like Modifier (SUMO) activating enzyme (SAE1)
Phenotypic characteristics of SAE1-positive patients: Prevalence of dysphagia and interstitial lung disease (ILD)
Cutaneous manifestations: From the classic Heliotrope rash to the Holster sign
The mechanism of micro-aspiration in the context of pharyngeal muscle weakness

sections.description: This section discusses the multi-modal treatment approach for severe dermatomyositis and the critical importance of malignancy screening in these patients.
subtopics: Acute management of airway-threatening swelling: High-dose pulse methylprednisolone
Steroid-sparing agents: Comparative use of Mycophenolate Mofetil, Rituximab, and Azathioprine
The role of Intravenous Immunoglobulin (IVIG) in refractory or severe myositis
Contraindications in myositis: Why Methotrexate may be avoided in patients with ILD
Malignancy screening guidelines: Applying IMACS criteria for high-risk dermatomyositis patients
Monitoring for remission: Normalization of CK and recovery of swallowing function
